category: Image Processing II: Color, Geometric Transforms, Feature Detection & Segmentation Measurements
description: Colour manipulation and analysis (quantization, dominant colours, replacement, tone mapping, alpha channels, chromaticity plots), geometric and projective transforms, feature and shape detection (lines, corners, ridges, contours, Radon transform), object localisation (ImagePosition, ImageBoundingBoxes, ImageContainsQ, faces), exposure/focus/panorama combination, and segmentation post-processing and measurements (components selection, geodesic and hit-miss morphology, Euler number, perimeter).

tools.name: ColorQuantize
tools.description: Reduces an image to n colours (default 16) by clustering, optionally with dithering, producing palette-style images for compression, posterization and pixel art; ColorConvert to "Grayscale" and ImageAdjust are the companions for tonal reduction.
tools.usage:
ColorQuantize[image]
ColorQuantize[image, n]
ColorQuantize[image, n, Dithering -> False]

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Number of colours in the output palette.

tools.example:
ColorQuantize[img, 8]
DominantColors[ColorQuantize[img, 4]]

tools.name: DominantColors
tools.description: Finds the n most prominent colours of an image (with optional minimum coverage and distance thresholds), returning colours or, with a property, their "Count", "Coverage" or "CoverageImage" masks. Use it for palette extraction, colour-based indexing and simple segmentation.
tools.usage:
DominantColors[image]
DominantColors[image, n]
DominantColors[image, n, "prop"]
DominantColors[image, n, {"Color", "Coverage"}, MinColorDistance -> 0.2]

tools.name: ColorReplace
tools.description: Replaces colours in an image within a tolerance of given colours (ColorReplace[img, col -> new, d]), ColorDetect makes a mask of pixels near a colour, ColorDistance computes perceptual distances (CIE76/CIE94/CIE2000 in Lab) between colours or between an image and a colour, and FindMatchingColor finds the closest named/palette colour. Together they implement colour-key masking, chroma keying and colour-based classification.
tools.usage:
ColorReplace[image, col -> newcol]
ColorReplace[image, col -> newcol, d]
ColorReplace[image, {col1 -> new1, col2 -> new2}]
ColorDetect[image, col]
ColorDetect[image, col, d]
ColorDistance[col1, col2]
ColorDistance[image, col, DistanceFunction -> "CIE2000"]
FindMatchingColor[col, {c1, c2, ...}]
tools.example:
mask = ColorDetect[img, Green, 0.25]; (* chroma key *)
ImageMultiply[img, ColorNegate[mask]]
ColorReplace[img, Green -> Transparent, 0.2]
ColorDistance[Red, Orange, DistanceFunction -> "CIE2000"]

tools.name: ColorToneMapping
tools.description: Compresses the dynamic range of HDR or high-contrast images for display (methods "Reinhard", "Drago", "Adaptive", ...), while ColorBalance corrects colour casts (automatically or toward a reference colour/white point) and BrightnessEqualize equalizes the brightness histogram. These are the global colour-correction tools before analysis or presentation.
tools.usage:
ColorToneMapping[image]
ColorToneMapping[image, s]
ColorToneMapping[image, s, Method -> "Reinhard"]
ColorBalance[image]
ColorBalance[image, refcolor]
ColorBalance[image, {refcolor, targetcolor}]
BrightnessEqualize[image]

parameters.name: refcolor
parameters.description: Colour that should become neutral (white balance).

tools.name: AlphaChannel
tools.description: Extracts the transparency channel of an image as a grayscale image; SetAlphaChannel attaches one (from a mask image or constant) and RemoveAlphaChannel flattens it against a background colour. Essential for compositing, PNG export with transparency and masking workflows with ImageCompose.
tools.usage:
AlphaChannel[image]
SetAlphaChannel[image, mask]
SetAlphaChannel[image, 0.5]
RemoveAlphaChannel[image]
RemoveAlphaChannel[image, background]

parameters.name: mask
parameters.description: Grayscale image or number giving opacity.

tools.name: ImageRecolor
tools.description: Recolours an image according to rules mapping regions (masks, colours or labelled components) to new colours or colour functions - e.g. colourize segmentation results over a grayscale image or replace hues; more flexible than Colorize because masks can be arbitrary images. ImageDemosaic reconstructs a full-colour image from a raw Bayer-pattern sensor image.
tools.usage:
ImageRecolor[image, mask -> color]
ImageRecolor[image, {mask1 -> col1, mask2 -> col2}]
ImageRecolor[image, mask -> ColorData["Rainbow"]]
ImageDemosaic[rawimage, "pattern"]

parameters.name: mask
parameters.description: Binary or grayscale image (values used as weights).

tools.name: PixelValue
tools.description: Reads the value(s) of an image at given pixel coordinates (integer positions, origin at bottom-left) and PixelValuePositions finds all positions with a given value (within tolerance); ReplacePixelValue sets pixels. ImageValue / ImageValuePositions / ReplaceImageValue are the equivalents in continuous image coordinates. Use them for point sampling and sparse edits.
tools.usage:
PixelValue[image, {x, y}]
PixelValue[image, {{x1, y1}, {x2, y2}, ...}]
PixelValuePositions[image, val]
PixelValuePositions[image, val, d]
ReplacePixelValue[image, {x, y} -> val]
ImageValuePositions[image, val]

parameters.name: val
parameters.description: Pixel value, colour or list of channel values.

tools.example:
PixelValue[img, {10, 20}]
white = PixelValuePositions[Binarize[img], 1]; Length[white]
ReplacePixelValue[img, {5, 5} -> Red]

tools.name: ImageScan
tools.description: Applies a function to every pixel value of an image (or to pixels in a region) for side effects such as accumulating statistics or Sow/Reap collection, without building a new image; ImageApply (listed) is the mapping form. ImageAccumulate sums a list of images (average with ImageAdd/ImageMultiply), used for noise reduction by frame averaging.
tools.usage:
ImageScan[f, image]
ImageScan[f, image, region]
ImageAccumulate[{img1, img2, ...}]
ImageAccumulate[imgs, "Mean"]

parameters.name: f
parameters.description: Function of the pixel value (list for multichannel).

tools.example:
counts = <||>; ImageScan[(counts[Round[#, 0.1]] = Lookup[counts, Round[#, 0.1], 0] + 1) &, gray]; KeySort[counts]
avg = ImageAccumulate[frames, "Mean"] (* noise-averaged frame *)

tools.name: ChromaticityPlot
tools.description: Plots colours or the colours of an image on a CIE chromaticity diagram (xy, u'v', or 3D with ChromaticityPlot3D), showing gamut coverage; ImageVectorscopePlot and ImageWaveformPlot are the video-engineering diagnostics (hue/saturation vectorscope, luminance waveform). Use them to analyse colour distribution and gamut of photographs and displays.
tools.usage:
ChromaticityPlot[image]
ChromaticityPlot[{col1, col2, ...}]
ChromaticityPlot[image, "CIEuv"]
ChromaticityPlot3D[image]
ImageVectorscopePlot[image]
ImageWaveformPlot[image]
tools.example:
ChromaticityPlot[photo, PlotStyle -> PointSize[Tiny]]
ImageVectorscopePlot[photo]

tools.name: ImageColorSpace
tools.description: Gives the colour space of an image ("RGB", "Grayscale", "CMYK", "LAB", "HSB", "XYZ" ...), which ColorConvert changes; ColorProfileData returns embedded ICC profile data, ColorQ tests whether an expression is a colour, RandomColor generates random colours (optionally from a colour distribution) and ReliefImage renders a height map with shading. Use ImageColorSpace to branch processing on colour vs grayscale input.
tools.usage:
ImageColorSpace[image]
ColorConvert[image, "LAB"]
ColorProfileData[image]
ColorQ[expr]
RandomColor[]
RandomColor[n]
RandomColor[Hue[_, 0.8, 0.9]]
ReliefImage[heights]

tools.name: FindThreshold
tools.description: Computes a global binarization threshold for an image or data by methods "Cluster" (Otsu, default), "Entropy", "Median", "Mean", "MinimumError", "Moments" - the value Binarize uses automatically; Threshold[data, spec] applies soft/hard/hyperbola thresholding to arbitrary arrays (denoising, sparsification). LocalAdaptiveBinarize binarizes with a locally varying threshold for uneven illumination.
tools.usage:
FindThreshold[image]
FindThreshold[image, Method -> "Entropy"]
Binarize[image, FindThreshold[image] + 0.05]
Threshold[data, {"Hard", delta}]
Threshold[data, {"Soft", delta}]
LocalAdaptiveBinarize[image, r]
LocalAdaptiveBinarize[image, r, {a, b, c}]
tools.example:
t = FindThreshold[scan, Method -> "MinimumError"];
bw = Binarize[scan, t]
LocalAdaptiveBinarize[unevenScan, 20]
Threshold[waveletCoeffs, {"Soft", 0.1}]

tools.name: ImagePerspectiveTransformation
tools.description: Applies a projective (homography) transformation given as a 3x3 matrix or TransformationFunction to an image - rectifying documents, correcting keystone distortion, mapping textures - with control of output size, DataRange and padding; ImageForwardTransformation maps pixels forward through an arbitrary function and ImageTransformation (listed) backward. FindGeometricTransform (listed) estimates the homography from point correspondences.
tools.usage:
ImagePerspectiveTransformation[image, m]
ImagePerspectiveTransformation[image, tf, size]
ImagePerspectiveTransformation[image, m, DataRange -> Full, Padding -> White]
ImageForwardTransformation[image, f]
ImageForwardTransformation[image, f, size]

parameters.name: f
parameters.description: Function mapping {x, y} to new coordinates.

tools.name: ImageLines
tools.description: Detects straight lines in an image with the Hough transform, returning line segments (or infinite lines) with optional thresholds on strength and distinctness; ImageCorners finds corner points (Harris/Shi-Tomasi) with CornerFilter as the underlying response filter, RidgeFilter enhances ridges/vessels and CrossingDetect finds zero crossings. These are the classical geometric feature detectors, complementing ImageKeypoints.
tools.usage:
ImageLines[image]
ImageLines[image, t]
ImageLines[image, t, d]
ImageLines[image, Method -> {"Hough", "Segmented" -> True}]
ImageCorners[image]
ImageCorners[image, r, t, d]
CornerFilter[image, r]
RidgeFilter[image]
RidgeFilter[image, sigma]
CrossingDetect[image]

tools.name: Radon
tools.description: Computes the Radon transform (sinogram) of an image - line integrals over all angles - and InverseRadon reconstructs an image from a sinogram by filtered back-projection; the mathematical core of CT reconstruction and a robust line-orientation detector. RadonTransform/InverseRadonTransform are the symbolic counterparts for functions.
tools.usage:
Radon[image]
Radon[image, {w, h}]
Radon[image, {w, h}, {thetamin, thetamax}]
InverseRadon[sinogram]
InverseRadon[sinogram, {w, h}, Method -> "Hamming"]

parameters.name: {w, h}
parameters.description: Output dimensions (angles x offsets for Radon).

tools.name: ContourDetect
tools.description: Finds iso-contours (level curves) of an image at a given level as a binary image, and EstimatedBackground estimates the slowly varying background of an image (for flat-field / illumination correction by subtraction or division); PeakDetect and MinDetect find local maxima/minima in arrays and images with scale control, the array-level relatives of MaxDetect. Used in microscopy and astronomy preprocessing.
tools.usage:
ContourDetect[image]
ContourDetect[image, level]
EstimatedBackground[image]
EstimatedBackground[image, r]
ImageSubtract[image, EstimatedBackground[image]]
PeakDetect[list]
PeakDetect[image, sigma, s, t]
MinDetect[image, h]

tools.name: ImageBoundingBoxes
tools.description: Detects objects of given categories (any concept from the image-identification knowledge base, or All) and returns bounding rectangles (with "Probability" and class labels on request); ImagePosition gives object centres, ImageContainsQ tests presence, and ImageCases (listed) crops the found objects. These build on the same neural detector as ImageContents and are the standard object-localisation API.
tools.usage:
ImageBoundingBoxes[image]
ImageBoundingBoxes[image, "category"]
ImageBoundingBoxes[image, {"cat1", "cat2"}]
ImageBoundingBoxes[image, category, {"BoundingBox", "Probability", "Concept"}]
ImagePosition[image, category]
ImageContainsQ[image, category]
ImageContainsQ[image, category, AcceptanceThreshold -> 0.7]

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: String such as "car", "person", an Entity["Concept", ...] or All.

tools.example:
boxes = ImageBoundingBoxes[street, "car"];
HighlightImage[street, boxes]
ImageContainsQ[street, "bicycle"]
ImagePosition[street, "traffic light"]

tools.name: FacialFeatures
tools.description: Extracts attributes of faces found in an image ("Age", "Gender", "Emotion", "Landmarks", "Descriptor", "Glasses"...) as an association per face; FaceRecognize (13.x) trains a classifier to identify people from example faces and FindFaces (listed) locates faces. Together they cover detection, recognition and attribute estimation using built-in neural models.
tools.usage:
FacialFeatures[image]
FacialFeatures[image, "prop"]
FacialFeatures[image, {"Age", "Emotion"}]
FaceRecognize[{face1 -> "Ann", face2 -> "Bob"}, image]
FaceRecognize[training, image, "BoundingBox" | "Probability"]

tools.name: FindImageShapes
tools.description: Finds geometric shapes ("Circle", "Ellipse", "Line", "Rectangle"...) in an image, returning graphics primitives with parameters, using edge detection plus Hough/RANSAC-style fitting; ImagePeriodogram shows the 2D power spectrum for detecting periodic textures and orientations. Useful for calibration targets, coins, wheels and machine-vision gauging.
tools.usage:
FindImageShapes[image, "Circle"]
FindImageShapes[image, "Ellipse", n]
FindImageShapes[image, {"Circle", "Line"}]
ImagePeriodogram[image]

tools.name: ImageStitch
tools.description: Stitches overlapping images into a panorama by finding correspondences, estimating transforms and blending (with options for the projection/canvas and blending method); ImageExposureCombine merges differently exposed shots into an HDR-like image and ImageFocusCombine merges a focus stack into an all-in-focus image. The three are the standard computational-photography combiners.
tools.usage:
ImageStitch[{img1, img2, ...}]
ImageStitch[imgs, "Cylindrical"]
ImageStitch[{{i11, i12}, {i21, i22}}] (* grid layout *)
ImageExposureCombine[{dark, mid, bright}]
ImageExposureCombine[imgs, "HDR"]
ImageFocusCombine[{focus1, focus2, ...}]
tools.example:
pano = ImageStitch[{Import["left.jpg"], Import["mid.jpg"], Import["right.jpg"]}, "Cylindrical"]
sharp = ImageFocusCombine[Import /@ FileNames["stack*.png"]]
tools.notes: ImageStitch introduced in 12.1; ImageExposureCombine and ImageFocusCombine in 11.3.

tools.name: ImageDistance
tools.description: Measures the distance between two images with a chosen metric ("EuclideanDistance" pixelwise, "MeanSquaredDistance", "MutualInformationVariation", "DifferenceNormalizedEntropy", "NormalizedCrossCorrelation", "Hash"-based ...), optionally at a given alignment offset; used for similarity search, registration quality and deduplication. ImageCooccurrence computes the gray-level co-occurrence matrix used for texture features.
tools.usage:
ImageDistance[img1, img2]
ImageDistance[img1, img2, DistanceFunction -> "MeanSquaredDistance"]
ImageDistance[img1, img2, {dx, dy}]
ImageCooccurrence[image, n]
ImageCooccurrence[image, n, {dx, dy}]

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Number of gray levels for the co-occurrence matrix.

tools.example:
ImageDistance[a, b, DistanceFunction -> "NormalizedCrossCorrelation"]
Nearest[images -> "Index", query, DistanceFunction -> ImageDistance]
glcm = ImageCooccurrence[texture, 16]; Total[Flatten[glcm^2]] (* energy *)

tools.name: SelectComponents
tools.description: Filters the components of a label matrix or segmented image by a property predicate ("Area" > 100, "Elongation", "Circularity"...) or by a ranking ("Count", largest n), keeping only matching components; DeleteSmallComponents and DeleteBorderComponents are the common special cases. Used after MorphologicalComponents/WatershedComponents to clean segmentations before ComponentMeasurements.
tools.usage:
SelectComponents[label, "prop", crit]
SelectComponents[label, #Area > 100 && #Circularity > 0.7 &]
SelectComponents[label, "Area", -3] (* 3 largest *)
DeleteSmallComponents[image]
DeleteSmallComponents[image, n]
DeleteBorderComponents[image]

parameters.name: crit
parameters.description: Predicate on the property value, or a count specification.

tools.name: ImageSegmentationComponents
tools.description: Neural-network based semantic/instance segmentation: labels each pixel of an image with object classes (from a trained model or the default set), returning a label matrix compatible with Colorize and ComponentMeasurements; GrowCutComponents segments interactively from seed markers, RegionBinarize grows a region from seeds by similarity and ChanVeseBinarize performs active-contour (Chan-Vese) segmentation. Choose them when thresholds and watersheds are insufficient.
tools.usage:
ImageSegmentationComponents[image]
ImageSegmentationComponents[image, {"person", "car"}]
GrowCutComponents[image, {fgMask, bgMask}]
RegionBinarize[image, marker, d]
ChanVeseBinarize[image]
ChanVeseBinarize[image, marker, {mu, lambda1, lambda2}]

parameters.name: marker
parameters.description: Seed image/mask or list of points.

tools.notes: ImageSegmentationComponents introduced in 13.1 and downloads a model on first use.

tools.name: GeodesicDilation
tools.description: Morphological reconstruction operators: GeodesicDilation[marker, mask] repeatedly dilates the marker but never beyond the mask (fills holes, extracts connected components touching seeds), GeodesicErosion is the dual, HitMissTransform detects exact local patterns with a structuring-element pair, and MorphologicalTransform applies an arbitrary function to each pixel neighbourhood. They implement reconstruction-based filtering, opening-by-reconstruction and pattern spotting.
tools.usage:
GeodesicDilation[marker, mask]
GeodesicDilation[marker, mask, n]
GeodesicErosion[marker, mask]
HitMissTransform[image, {ker1, ker2}]
HitMissTransform[image, ker]
MorphologicalTransform[image, f]
MorphologicalTransform[image, "Perimeter" | "Skeleton" | "Fill" | ...]

parameters.name: ker
parameters.description: Structuring element with 1 (foreground) and 0 (background) entries; -1/missing ignored.

tools.example:
(* remove components not touching the seeds *)
seeds = ImageMultiply[bw, seedMask];
kept = GeodesicDilation[seeds, bw]
(* fill holes by reconstruction from the border *)
filled = ColorNegate[GeodesicDilation[ImageSubtract[ConstantImage[1, ImageDimensions[bw]], bw] // ImagePad[#, -1] &, ColorNegate[bw]]]
HitMissTransform[bw, {{{1, 1, 1}, {0, 1, 0}, {0, 1, 0}}, {{0, 0, 0}, {1, 0, 1}, {1, 0, 1}}}] (* T-junction pattern *)

tools.name: MorphologicalEulerNumber
tools.description: Gives the Euler number (components minus holes) of a binary image and MorphologicalPerimeter the perimeter image/length, with ComponentMeasurements (listed) providing the full per-component property set ("Area", "Centroid", "BoundingBox", "Perimeter", "Circularity", "Elongation", "Orientation", "EquivalentDiskRadius", "ConvexArea", "Holes", "Mask", "Image", "MeanIntensity", "Neighbors"...). Use these for shape statistics in microscopy, materials and quality inspection.
tools.usage:
MorphologicalEulerNumber[image]
MorphologicalPerimeter[image]
ComponentMeasurements[label, "prop"]
ComponentMeasurements[label, {"Area", "Centroid", "Circularity"}]
ComponentMeasurements[{image, label}, "MeanIntensity"]
ComponentMeasurements[label, "prop", crit, "PropertyAssociation" | "Dataset"]

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: Label matrix from MorphologicalComponents etc., or a binary image.

tools.name: ImageMarker
tools.description: Marks points (or a list of point -> marker specs) on an image for interactive seeding of WatershedComponents, GrowCutComponents and RegionBinarize; in notebooks it also displays markers over the image. ImageClip clips pixel values to a range (with optional replacement values), a fast way to saturate outliers before analysis.
tools.usage:
ImageMarker[image, {pt1, pt2, ...}]
ImageMarker[image, {pt1 -> 1, pt2 -> 2}]
WatershedComponents[image, ImageMarker[image, seeds]]
ImageClip[image]
ImageClip[image, {min, max}]
ImageClip[image, {min, max}, {vmin, vmax}]

parameters.name: pts
parameters.description: Pixel coordinates of markers (with optional labels).

tools.name: ImageResolution
tools.description: Option of Import/Export and Rasterize giving the resolution in dpi (stored as metadata in PNG/TIFF/JPEG and used when rasterizing graphics); Export[..., ImageResolution -> 300] is the standard way to produce print-quality figures. Together with ImageSize (pixels or Scaled) and "CompressionLevel"/"ColorSpace" export options it controls raster output quality.
tools.usage:
Export["fig.png", plot, ImageResolution -> 300]
Export["fig.tiff", img, ImageResolution -> 600, "ColorSpace" -> "CMYK"]
Rasterize[expr, ImageResolution -> 200]
Import["fig.png", "ImageResolution"]
tools.example:
Export["figure1.png", Plot[Sin[x], {x, 0, 6}, ImageSize -> 600], ImageResolution -> 300]
Import["figure1.png", "ImageResolution"] (* 300. *)

tools.name: MorphologicalTransform
tools.description: Applies a function (or a named transform such as "Perimeter", "Skeleton", "Fill", "Remove", "Majority", "Clean", "Bridge", "Diag", "Shrink", "Thicken"...) to the neighbourhood of every pixel of a binary image, optionally iterated n times - the general engine behind Thinning, Pruning and the classic MATLAB-style bwmorph operations. Use named transforms for standard clean-up and a custom function for bespoke local rules.
tools.usage:
MorphologicalTransform[image, f]
MorphologicalTransform[image, "name"]
MorphologicalTransform[image, {"name1", "name2"}]
MorphologicalTransform[image, f, n]
MorphologicalTransform[image, f, Infinity] (* until stable *)

parameters.name: f
parameters.description: Function of the 3x3 (or larger) neighbourhood matrix returning 0/1, or a named transform.

tools.example:
MorphologicalTransform[bw, {"Fill", "Clean", "Majority"}]
MorphologicalTransform[bw, "Perimeter"]
MorphologicalTransform[bw, Boole[Total[Flatten[#]] >= 5] &, 3]

tools.name: HitMissTransform
tools.description: Detects pixels whose neighbourhood exactly matches a foreground/background template pair (kernel with 1 = must be on, 0 = must be off, other entries ignored), the basic pattern-spotting morphological operator used for corner and end-point detection in skeletons and for template matching in binary images; supports lists of kernels and Padding control.
tools.usage:
HitMissTransform[image, ker]
HitMissTransform[image, {ker1, ker2, ...}]
HitMissTransform[image, ker, Padding -> 0]
tools.example:
endpoints = HitMissTransform[Thinning[bw], {{{-1, -1, -1}, {0, 1, 0}, {-1, -1, -1}} /. -1 -> Missing[], ...}]
HitMissTransform[bw, {{0, 0, 0}, {0, 1, 0}, {0, 0, 0}}] (* isolated pixels *)

tools.name: ImageCooccurrence
tools.description: Computes the gray-level co-occurrence matrix of an image for n quantization levels and a pixel offset (or several), the basis of Haralick texture features (energy, contrast, homogeneity, entropy) used in texture classification, medical image analysis and remote sensing.
tools.usage:
ImageCooccurrence[image, n]
ImageCooccurrence[image, n, {dx, dy}]
ImageCooccurrence[image, n, {{dx1, dy1}, {dx2, dy2}, ...}]

tools.name: LocalAdaptiveBinarize
tools.description: Binarizes an image using a threshold computed in a neighbourhood of radius r around each pixel (mean/standard-deviation based, with coefficients {a, b, c}), so that documents and micrographs with uneven illumination binarize cleanly where a global Binarize fails. Related: Binarize with a function, FindThreshold, MorphologicalBinarize.
tools.usage:
LocalAdaptiveBinarize[image, r]
LocalAdaptiveBinarize[image, r, {a, b, c}]
LocalAdaptiveBinarize[image, r, Padding -> "Fixed"]
tools.example:
text = LocalAdaptiveBinarize[scan, 25, {1, 0, -0.02}];
TextRecognize[text]

tools.name: ImageForwardTransformation
tools.description: Maps every pixel of an image forward through a function f[{x, y}] -> {x', y'} (in image coordinates, 0-1 by default), scattering pixels onto the output canvas with resampling; the forward counterpart of ImageTransformation (which samples backward and is preferred when the inverse map is known). Use it for lens-distortion simulation, warps and morphing when only the forward map is available.
tools.usage:
ImageForwardTransformation[image, f]
ImageForwardTransformation[image, f, size]
ImageForwardTransformation[image, f, DataRange -> Full, Padding -> White]

parameters.name: f
parameters.description: Function from {x, y} to new coordinates.

tools.example:
ImageForwardTransformation[img, {#[[1]]^2, #[[2]]} &]
ImageForwardTransformation[img, RotationTransform[0.3, {0.5, 0.5}], Padding -> Transparent]

tools.name: ImageAccumulate
tools.description: Adds a list of images pixelwise (clipping or scaling as specified), giving frame averaging for noise reduction ("Mean"), exposure stacking, motion trails and heat maps of detections; images must have the same dimensions (ImageResize/ImagePad first). ImageAdd/ImageMultiply are the two-image forms.
tools.usage:
ImageAccumulate[{img1, img2, ...}]
ImageAccumulate[imgs, "Mean"]
ImageAccumulate[imgs, "Clip" | "Scale"]

parameters.name: imgs
parameters.description: List of images of equal size and type.
